---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# vc-dr-apply.sh: apply a source dual repo's rules and agent files, and its skeletons, as its
# working copy holds them or as landed, to a bare dual workspace that `vc-x1 init` made, new or
# adopted. It may live anywhere, ~/bin included, since the skeletons come from the source. A
# first cut: it writes only new files, refuses when any existing file would change, and commits
# nothing.
set -euo pipefail

die() {
    echo "vc-dr-apply: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: vc-dr-apply.sh [--to DIR] [--landed] [--rev REV] [--agent-rev REV] [--skel DIR]
                      [--lang NAME] [--dry-run] SOURCE [AGENT_SOURCE]
       vc-dr-apply.sh --lang [--skel DIR] [SOURCE]

Apply what SOURCE holds, one tree per repo, to the dual workspace DIR, made by `vc-x1 init`:

  SOURCE                a dual workspace, its agent repo found by its .vc-config.md
  SOURCE AGENT_SOURCE   a work repo and an agent repo, each given

  --to DIR         the workspace written [default: .]
  --landed         both repos at main, what landed, rather than the working copies
  --rev REV        the source work repo's commit, any jj revision naming one [default: @,
                   the working copy as on disk, which jj snapshots first]
  --agent-rev REV  the source agent repo's commit [default: @, as --rev]
  --skel DIR       the skeletons, a directory holding vc-dr-apply-base/ and vc-dr-apply-lang/,
                   as on disk [default: the source work repo's scripts/ at --rev, else this
                   script's own directory, symlinks resolved]
  --lang NAME      also apply the language skeleton vc-dr-apply-lang/NAME/, its [validate]
                   table appended to DIR's .vc-config.md; --lang alone lists them
  --dry-run        print the plan and write nothing

The default is the active version, the working copy with what it has not committed, so a test
repo gets the rules being worked on. --landed takes the trunk's, and --rev or --agent-rev, given
after it, overrides it for that repo. The skeletons follow the work repo's revision, so they
match the agent-files they come with.

From the work repo: AGENTS.md, agent-data/, and LICENSE-*. From the agent repo: LICENSE-*,
README.md, its first line renamed for DIR's agent repo, and memory/MEMORY.md, each when present.
From vc-dr-apply-base/: work/, the work repo's skeletons, {name} the workspace's directory name
and {module} it with each '-' an '_', in file contents and paths, and gitignore-lines, the
.gitignore lines.

A language skeleton, vc-dr-apply-lang/NAME/, holds the project's starting files, written like the
others, and three files that are not: validate.toml, the [validate] table appended to
.vc-config.md, refused when it has one already; gitignore-lines, more .gitignore lines; and
replaces, the base skeleton's paths it supersedes, left out, version.toml when the build system
holds the version. A new language is a new directory with a validate.toml.

Both repos of DIR must have an empty `@`, so every write is a diff `jj restore` undoes. Each
path is new, identical, or differs, judged on disk. New is written and identical skipped, and
any path that differs refuses the whole apply, nothing written. `.gitignore` takes the lines it
lacks. Nothing is committed: the end names the commit to make after review.
EOF
}

script_dir=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
to=.
rev=@
agent_rev=@
skel_opt=
dry_run=0
lang=
list_langs=0
sources=()
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --to | --rev | --agent-rev | --skel)
        (($# >= 2)) || die "$1 takes a value"
        case $1 in
        --to) to=$2 ;;
        --rev) rev=$2 ;;
        --agent-rev) agent_rev=$2 ;;
        --skel) skel_opt=$2 ;;
        esac
        shift 2
        ;;
    --dry-run)
        dry_run=1
        shift
        ;;
    --landed)
        rev=main
        agent_rev=main
        shift
        ;;
    --lang)
        # A language name has no '/', so a path after --lang is the SOURCE to list from.
        if (($# < 2)) || [[ $2 == -* || $2 == */* || $2 == . || $2 == .. ]]; then
            list_langs=1
            shift
        else
            lang=$2
            shift 2
        fi
        ;;
    -h | --help)
        usage
        exit 0
        ;;
    -*) die "unknown option '$1', see --help" ;;
    *)
        sources+=("$1")
        shift
        ;;
    esac
done
if ((list_langs)); then
    ((${#sources[@]} || ${#skel_opt})) || die "--lang alone lists from SOURCE or --skel DIR, see --help"
else
    ((${#sources[@]} == 1 || ${#sources[@]} == 2)) || die "takes SOURCE or SOURCE AGENT_SOURCE, see --help"
fi

# The agent repo a workspace's .vc-config.md names, absolute.
agent_of() {
    local ws=$1 dir
    [[ -f $ws/.vc-config.md ]] || die "'$ws' has no .vc-config.md"
    dir=$(sed -n '/^\[repos\]/,/^\[/{s/^agent *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p}' "$ws/.vc-config.md" | head -n1)
    [[ -n $dir ]] || die "'$ws' declares no [repos] agent: it is not a dual workspace"
    case $dir in
    /*) echo "$dir" ;;
    *) echo "$ws/$dir" ;;
    esac
}

# The one commit REV names in REPO, refused unless it is exactly one. A jj command snapshots the
# working copy first, so `@` is the tree on disk, and jj keeps its commit in the git store, where
# `git archive` reads it.
commit_of() {
    local repo=$1 r=$2 sha
    sha=$(jj -R "$repo" log --no-graph -r "$r" -T 'commit_id ++ "\n"')
    [[ -n $sha && $(wc -l <<<"$sha") -eq 1 ]] || die "'$r' must name exactly one commit in '$repo'"
    echo "$sha"
}

# Whether PATH exists in REPO at SHA.
in_commit() {
    git -C "$1" cat-file -e "$2:$3" 2>/dev/null
}

absolute() {
    [[ -d $1 ]] || die "'$1' is not a directory"
    (cd "$1" && pwd)
}

# What a revision is, for the plan and the commit body: the working copy by its change id, which
# survives the snapshot's rewrites, or the revision as given.
named() {
    local repo=$1 r=$2 at=$3
    if [[ $r == @ ]]; then
        echo "its working copy, change $(jj -R "$repo" log --no-graph -r @ -T 'change_id.short(12)')"
    else
        echo "${at:0:12} ($r)"
    fi
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vc-dr-apply.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# --- The source, and the commit of each repo ---------------------------------------------------

if ((${#sources[@]})); then
    src=$(absolute "${sources[0]}")
    if ((${#sources[@]} == 2)); then
        src_agent=$(absolute "${sources[1]}")
    else
        src_agent=$(agent_of "$src")
    fi
    for repo in "$src" "$src_agent"; do
        [[ -d $repo/.jj ]] || die "the source '$repo' is not a jj repo"
    done
    sha=$(commit_of "$src" "$rev")
    agent_sha=$(commit_of "$src_agent" "$agent_rev")
    src_at=$(named "$src" "$rev" "$sha")
    agent_at=$(named "$src_agent" "$agent_rev" "$agent_sha")
fi

# --- The skeletons -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if [[ -n $skel_opt ]]; then
    skel=$(absolute "$skel_opt")
    skel_from="--skel $skel"
elif ((${#sources[@]})) && in_commit "$src" "$sha" scripts/vc-dr-apply-base; then
    mkdir -p "$tmp/skel"
    paths=(scripts/vc-dr-apply-base)
    if in_commit "$src" "$sha" scripts/vc-dr-apply-lang; then paths+=(scripts/vc-dr-apply-lang); fi
    git -C "$src" archive "$sha" "${paths[@]}" | tar -x -C "$tmp/skel"
    skel=$tmp/skel/scripts
    skel_from="the source's scripts/ at $src_at"
else
    skel=$script_dir
    skel_from="this script's directory, $script_dir, the source having none"
fi
langs_dir=$skel/vc-dr-apply-lang

# The language skeletons, one per directory with a validate.toml.
langs() {
    local d
    for d in "$langs_dir"/*/; do
        if [[ -f $d/validate.toml ]]; then basename "$d"; fi
    done
}

if ((list_langs)); then
    echo "vc-dr-apply: the language skeletons, from $skel_from:"
    langs | sed 's/^/  /'
    exit 0
fi
[[ -d $skel/vc-dr-apply-base/work ]] || die "no vc-dr-apply-base/work in $skel_from, see --skel"
lang_dir=
if [[ -n $lang ]]; then
    lang_dir=$langs_dir/$lang
    [[ -f $lang_dir/validate.toml ]] ||
        die "no language skeleton '$lang' in $skel_from, the choices: $(langs | paste -sd ' ')"
fi

# --- The target workspace ----------------------------------------------------------------------

ws=$(absolute "$to")
agent=$(agent_of "$ws")
[[ -d $agent/.jj ]] || die "the agent repo '$agent' is not a jj repo"
[[ $ws != "$src" ]] || die "the source and the target are the same workspace"
name=$(basename "$ws")
agent_name=$(sed -n '/^\[remote\]/,/^\[/{s/^agent-repo *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p}' "$ws/.vc-config.md" | head -n1)
[[ -n $agent_name ]] || agent_name=$name.agent-session

for repo in "$ws" "$agent"; do
    [[ -z $(jj -R "$repo" diff --summary) ]] ||
        die "'$repo' has uncommitted changes: commit or restore them first, so the apply is one diff"
done

# --- Stage what would be written ---------------------------------------------------------------

stage=$tmp/stage
mkdir -p "$stage/work" "$stage/agent"

# Archive the PATHS present in REPO at SHA into DEST.
take() {
    local repo=$1 at=$2 dest=$3 p
    shift 3
    local present=()
    for p in "$@"; do
        if in_commit "$repo" "$at" "$p"; then present+=("$p"); fi
    done
    ((${#present[@]})) || return 0
    git -C "$repo" archive "$at" "${present[@]}" | tar -x -C "$dest"
}

in_commit "$src" "$sha" AGENTS.md || die "the source work repo has no AGENTS.md at ${sha:0:12}"
take "$src" "$sha" "$stage/work" AGENTS.md agent-data LICENSE-APACHE LICENSE-MIT
take "$src_agent" "$agent_sha" "$stage/agent" LICENSE-APACHE LICENSE-MIT README.md memory/MEMORY.md
if [[ -f $stage/agent/README.md ]]; then
    sed -i "1s|.*|# $agent_name|" "$stage/agent/README.md"
fi
cp -R "$skel/vc-dr-apply-base/work/." "$stage/work/"
if [[ -n $lang_dir ]]; then
    if [[ -f $lang_dir/replaces ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r x; do
            if [[ -n $x ]]; then rm -f "$stage/work/$x"; fi
        done <"$lang_dir/replaces"
    fi
    cp -R "$lang_dir/." "$stage/work/"
    rm -f "$stage/work/validate.toml" "$stage/work/gitignore-lines" "$stage/work/replaces"
fi
module=${name//-/_}
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    sed -i "s|{name}|$name|g; s|{module}|$module|g" "$f"
done < <(grep -rlZ -e '{name}' -e '{module}' "$stage/work" || true)
# A path naming {name} or {module} is renamed, the deepest first.
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    base=$(basename "$f")
    base=${base//\{name\}/$name}
    mv "$f" "$(dirname "$f")/${base//\{module\}/$module}"
done < <(find "$stage/work" -depth \( -name '*{name}*' -o -name '*{module}*' \) -print0)
[[ -z $(find "$stage" -type l) ]] || die "the staged files hold a symlink, refused"

# --- The plan ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

new=()
same=()
differs=()

# Why REL cannot be written under DEST: it, or a directory it needs, is a symlink or the wrong
# kind of entry. Empty when it can.
blocked() {
    local dest=$1 rel=$2 path=$1 part
    local parts
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<<"$rel"
    for part in "${parts[@]::${#parts[@]}-1}"; do
        path=$path/$part
        if [[ -L $path || (-e $path && ! -d $path) ]]; then
            echo "$part is not a directory"
            return
        fi
    done
    if [[ -L $dest/$rel ]]; then
        echo "a symlink"
    elif [[ -d $dest/$rel ]]; then
        echo "a directory"
    fi
}

plan_side() {
    local side=$1 dest=$2 f rel why
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        rel=${f#"$stage/$side/"}
        why=$(blocked "$dest" "$rel")
        if [[ -n $why ]]; then
            differs+=("$side $rel ($why)")
        elif [[ ! -e $dest/$rel ]]; then
            new+=("$side $rel")
        elif cmp -s "$f" "$dest/$rel"; then
            same+=("$side $rel")
        else
            differs+=("$side $rel")
        fi
    done < <(find "$stage/$side" -type f -print0 | sort -z)
}

plan_side work "$ws"
plan_side agent "$agent"

ignore_add=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ -f $ws/.gitignore ]] && grep -qxF -- "$line" "$ws/.gitignore" && continue
    ignore_add+=("$line")
done < <(cat "$skel/vc-dr-apply-base/gitignore-lines" ${lang_dir:+"$lang_dir/gitignore-lines"} 2>/dev/null)

# The [validate] table a language skeleton brings, refused when the config has one.
validate_add=
if [[ -n $lang_dir ]]; then
    if grep -q '^\[validate\]' "$ws/.vc-config.md"; then
        differs+=("work .vc-config.md (it has a [validate] table, so $lang's is not added)")
    else
        validate_add=$(cat "$lang_dir/validate.toml")
    fi
fi

echo "vc-dr-apply: from $src at $src_at, its agent repo at $agent_at"
echo "vc-dr-apply: skeletons from $skel_from"
echo "vc-dr-apply: onto $ws, agent repo $agent"
for x in ${new[@]+"${new[@]}"}; do echo "  new       $x"; done
for x in ${same[@]+"${same[@]}"}; do echo "  identical $x"; done
for x in ${differs[@]+"${differs[@]}"}; do echo "  differs   $x"; done
for x in ${ignore_add[@]+"${ignore_add[@]}"}; do echo "  ignore    work .gitignore + $x"; done
[[ -z $validate_add ]] || echo "  config    work .vc-config.md + [validate], the $lang skeleton's"

if ((${#differs[@]})); then
    die "${#differs[@]} path(s) differ from what would be written, so nothing was written"
fi
if ((dry_run)); then
    echo "vc-dr-apply: dry run, nothing written"
    exit 0
fi

# --- Apply -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

for x in ${new[@]+"${new[@]}"}; do
    side=${x%% *}
    rel=${x#* }
    if [[ $side == work ]]; then dest=$ws; else dest=$agent; fi
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest/$rel")"
    cp "$stage/$side/$rel" "$dest/$rel"
done
if ((${#ignore_add[@]})); then
    printf '%s\n' "${ignore_add[@]}" >>"$ws/.gitignore"
fi
if [[ -n $validate_add ]]; then
    printf '\nThe validation commands, from the %s language skeleton\n```toml\n%s\n```\n' \
        "$lang" "$validate_add" >>"$ws/.vc-config.md"
fi

echo "vc-dr-apply: applied, nothing committed. custom.md is written and gitignored, local."
echo "--- work repo"
(cd "$ws" && jj diff --stat)
echo "--- agent repo"
(cd "$agent" && jj diff --stat)
src_name=$(basename "$src")
cat <<EOF
Review both diffs, then commit, for example:
  vc-x1 commit -s b -R $ws --title "chore: apply $src_name's rules" \\
    --body "A bare workspace has no rules to work by.

Solution: $src_name's agent-files and agent files, from $src_name at $src_at and its agent repo at $agent_at."
EOF
---

for x in ${differs[@]+"${differs[@]}"}; do echo "  differs   $x"; done
for x in ${ignore_add[@]+"${ignore_add[@]}"}; do echo "  ignore    work .gitignore + $x"; done
[[ -z $validate_add ]] || echo "  config    work .vc-config.md + [validate], the $lang skeleton's"

if ((${#differs[@]})); then
    die "${#differs[@]} path(s) differ from what would be written, so nothing was written"
fi
if ((dry_run)); then
    echo "vc-dr-apply: dry run, nothing written"
    exit 0
fi

# --- Apply -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

for x in ${new[@]+"${new[@]}"}; do
    side=${x%% *}
    rel=${x#* }
    if [[ $side == work ]]; then dest=$ws; else dest=$agent; fi
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest/$rel")"
    cp "$stage/$side/$rel" "$dest/$rel"
done
if ((${#ignore_add[@]})); then
    printf '%s\n' "${ignore_add[@]}" >>"$ws/.gitignore"
fi
if [[ -n $validate_add ]]; then
    printf '\nThe validation commands, from the %s language skeleton\n```toml\n%s\n```\n' \
        "$lang" "$validate_add" >>"$ws/.vc-config.md"
fi

echo "vc-dr-apply: applied, nothing committed. custom.md is written and gitignored, local."
echo "--- work repo"
(cd "$ws" && jj diff --stat)
echo "--- agent repo"
(cd "$agent" && jj diff --stat)
src_name=$(basename "$src")
cat <<EOF
Review both diffs, then commit, for example:
  vc-x1 commit -s b -R $ws --title "chore: apply $src_name's rules" \\
    --body "A bare workspace has no rules to work by.

Solution: $src_name's agent-files and agent files, from $src_name at $src_at and its agent repo at $agent_at."
EOF
---

719:## Closed
726:### agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9
## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). Earlier cycles are in the landmark commit's copy
of this section, and the cycles before the rule in the frozen [notes/chores/](notes/chores) and
[notes/done.md](notes/done.md).

### agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9

#### Problem

The family's agreed set is v0.2.9 and ours is v0.2.8, one proposal behind. vc-x1 asked for the
adoption on the thread `m-11` in `../vc-x1-messages`, its set at `12a73d7135ab`, replacing the
v0.2.8 request on `m-9`. What v0.2.9 brings:

- The per-rung flow gains a step 0, a sync of both repos at the rung's start, required at the
  opening and the closing, optional between, and `## Sync` lists the closing among its moments.
- The Validate step gains a rule: a failure is read and its cause named before validation runs
  again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported and given a Todo entry.
- The session lock line leaves `custom.md`. The lock stays off, and `agent-data/session-lock.md`
  still says how to turn it on.

#### Solution

A single-step adoption, the source's set taken whole by `vc-x1 agent-files copy -c ../vc-x1`:
`agent-data/agent-files-v0.2.8` renamed to `agent-data/agent-files-v0.2.9`, `AGENTS.md` and
`rationale.md` changed, and `custom.md` taken as the family's, its session lock line gone.

#### Acceptance check

`vc-x1 agent-files diff -c ../vc-x1` reports 0 of 12 differing, `vc-x1 agent-files version` prints
`v0.2.9`, and `agent-data` holds no `agent-files-v0.2.8`.

Passed (2026-10-15): the diff reports all twelve files the same, the version prints `v0.2.9`, and
`ls agent-data` lists `agent-files-v0.2.9` alone among the version files.

#### Deliberation

- Single-step: a copy and no design, so one commit carrying the bare version and no dev rename, as
  the v0.2.8 adoption did.
- Adoptions copy and bump nothing: the version file is the source's ([Agent-files
  version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
- `custom.md` is taken as vc-x1 wrote it, so the `-c` stays on the copy and the diff: the one change
  drops the session lock line, and the lock was already off.
- The reference checkout, `../vc-x1`, was at `12a73d7135ab` when the copy ran, the commit `m-11`
  names, its set v0.2.9. The installed `vc-x1` is 0.85.0, past the 0.84.30 that `m-11` asks for.
- This cycle ran under the v0.2.8 rules it replaces, so its opening had no step 0 by that name. Its
  opening sync was the same act.
- The messages owed wait for the Land, so the reply on `m-11` links the landed commit, and one reply
  answers `m-9` and `m-11` both, since `m-11` replaces `m-9`.
- `## Waiting` is `_None._`, nothing to promote.

#### Ladder

- agent-files(adoption): v0.2.9 (done)

# References

### Fix bug Y

What is wrong and where [[1]].

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
```

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **rungs**: a `#### Rungs` heading over the rung subsections, the ladder itself being `zTOC.md`'s
  ([zTOC format](#ztoc-format)), made by the tool from the subsections' headings, so a rung is
  written once, as its heading: one rung per step, `- 2 (done) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`: the
  rung's number, its position in the ladder from `0`, then the marker, `(done)` or `(current)`,
  both first so they read down their columns, and a rung not yet started has neither, and an inline
  link so the ladder is one list with nothing beside it to keep in step, its line as long as the
  title makes it. A rung is `(done)` when a commit of its title is on the cycle's branch and
  `(current)` when it is the first without one, so no marker is typed. `<title>` is the rung's
  commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per [Conventional-commit
  shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a `## Todo` entry is retitled as
  its cycle title before `cycle --open` moves it. The first rung is `<cycle title> opening` and the
  last `<cycle title> closing`, linked like the rest

`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
`_None._`.

30	`vc-x1 cycle`, whose stages are its flags ([Cycle protocol](#cycle-protocol)). Its shape is its

33	the user decides otherwise.

42	a trapezoid's `--trapezoid <target>`, stored nowhere, and never assumed, since a bookmark made is
43	likely, not certainly, the one a cycle lands on. `main` by convention, and a release branch is a
44	target as much as `main` is.
45

47	rung or after the closing, and leaves the cycle a draft. The publish is the Land's push of the
48	target, which makes the cycle permanent and removes the draft.

51	whose second is the cycle's ladder ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)). Names

60	not when following one.

...

67	The section is the rule, the sentence its handle. None is absolute: a rule bends only when the
68	user says so explicitly, at the moment or as a scoped delegation ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask) is
69	the path), and the exception is recorded in the cycle's records, naming what the bend covers and
70	what it does not, so a waiver over a cycle's pushes says whether Land is inside it. No rule bends
71	silently.

74	  anything in the agent-files, and it holds what is local to the workspace

77	  left as found until the user says how to proceed ([Acquaint](#acquaint)).
78	- Sync where `main` matters: a look at acquaint and a sync at the opening, the closing, and Land,
79	  each reported, and a repo held back stops the step ([Sync](#sync)).

81	  writes, and another repo's rules bind only by delegation ([A session's rules are its own
82	  agent-files](#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)).
83	- Bookmark per cycle: a cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, and `main` advances
84	  only when the cycle lands ([Cycles run on a bookmark](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)).
85	- Shape named, count checked: the closing names the cycle single-step or multi-step, its branch's
86	  commit count checks the name, and a ladder lands as a trapezoid, never squashed ([Cycle
87	  shape](#cycle-shape)).
88	- Local by default: a cycle's commits stay on this machine until the Land, and the user decides when
89	  each side commits and publishes ([A cycle is local by default](#a-cycle-is-local-by-default)).
90	- Read the step before the action: [The per-rung flow](#the-per-rung-flow) before commit work,
91	  [Before any push](#before-any-push) before a push, from the file, not from memory.
92	- Commit by the tool: a cycle's commits are made only by `vc-x1 cycle`, a rung by `--commit` and the
93	  closing by `--close` ([Committing vs pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)).
94	- The ladder is the tool's: a rung is written once, as its heading under `#### Rungs`, and no
95	  marker is typed ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)).
96	- The version is the project's: `vc-x1` never bumps it, and refuses a commit that leaves it
97	  unchanged when the config asks ([The per-rung flow](#the-per-rung-flow)).
98	- Approval per push: only a push publishes, and every push needs the user's explicit approval, or an
99	  explicit waiver ([Before any push](#before-any-push)).
100	- Hard stop after the final push: after the turn's final push nothing until the user speaks,
101	  unless an explicit waiver ([At rest](#at-rest)).
102	- One command per invocation: no bundled steps, except a genuine pipeline or a tight pair
103	  ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
104	- Exit status: the command under test runs bare and last, `set -o pipefail` first when piped, and
105	  `bash-guard.sh` denies the masks it can see ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
106	- Long output: a command known to print more than the Bash tool returns keeps its output in a file
107	  and shows its tail, and a pass is its exit status ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
108	- Stop and ask: on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes
109	  on a simple task has produced no progress ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask)).
110	- Changing the agent-files: a change to the rules is tried in the local copy, then proposed as one
111	  set of diffs, which an adopter accepts as is, negotiates, or declines ([Changing the
112	  agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)).
113	- jj, not git: version-control operations use jj ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
114	- No hand-written trailers: the tool stamps the trailers, never write one by hand
115	  ([ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).

check() {
  local bad=0 s e m c
  for s in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if [[ ! -f $dest/$s ]]; then
      echo "hooks: missing    $dest/$s"
      bad=1
    elif ! cmp -s "$here/$s" "$dest/$s"; then
      echo "hooks: differs    $dest/$s"
      bad=1
    fi
  done
  while IFS='|' read -r e m c; do
    if ! registered "$e" "$m" "$c"; then
      echo "hooks: unregistered $e${m:+ [$m]}: $c"
      bad=1
    fi
  done < <(registrations)
  if ((bad)); then
    echo "hooks: not installed, run: bash $here/hooks.sh install"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "hooks: ${#scripts[@]} hooks installed and registered"
}

====
# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

The project's own layer over the other agent-files (see
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd)). Loaded last. On conflict, this file wins.

supersedes.

### Commit-body form

The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is two plain paragraphs, and the
rung's subsection in the record holds the full account, so the breakdown is written once.

- **The problem**, and it defines any word the title assumes. It is *this commit's*, never the
  cycle's: a body whose problem outruns what the diff resolves is describing something larger than
  the commit.
- **The solution**, opening "Solution:", ending with the pointer to the record where it is at that
  commit, "See details in TODO.md." No bullets, so a `--body` flag cannot mistake it for an option.
- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
  its body names the cycle by its title, "Opens the cycle ..." or "Closes the cycle ...", with the
  same pointer after it.

Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

# Commit model

specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

Solution: a loader finds and reads the file and a parser takes text and
returns the schema, so a test hands the parser a string, and `main` gets
the schema from one call. See details in TODO.md.
```

The first paragraph states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes.
The second opens "Solution:" and ends with the pointer, and nothing names a file that the diff
already lists.

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". See details in
TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body names the cycle by its title and points at
its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

input.description: Show vc-x1 push usage

content.content:
vc-x1 0.85.22+bd1d20bf1131

Publish a rung's pair: the work commit on its bookmark and the
agent commit on `main`. Push carries no description and writes
none, so what was reviewed is what goes out.

`commit` makes the pair, both commits now (-s b) or the work
half with its trailer naming the agent @ (-s w). Push publishes
the work @-, so new work in @ is left as it is, and it refuses
a work @- with no `ochid:` trailer, which is not a pair's commit.

The halves are independent, each side naming the other by
change id, which no push moves. -s b makes every local step
first, then publishes the work repo and then the agent repo,
the order `squash-push -s b` publishes in:
  - agent  complete the partner by the state found: commit the
           journal as the partner when pending or the agent
           repo changed
  - work   restamp the unpublished work commit if its trailer
           does not name the partner, then set and push
           <bookmark>
  - agent  publish main, the journal folded into a committed
           partner unless it is already published

-s is required: `b` both halves, `a` the agent half, `w` the work
half, `p` a plain repo's @- on its bookmark. -R is optional and
says where. --bookmark is the line's unless named, as a check or
as a new name created at @- and pushed tracked.

-r names another commit, already made, and a name alone goes out
for it, no pair: the one bookmark at it, or --bookmark's, that
bookmark or a new one created there. The working copy and the
root are refused, and so is a REV of several commits.

Every argument is a flag: the old positional is refused, naming
--bookmark or -r, the one it was.

A push that would be forced, a published commit rewritten, is
warned of and asked about before anything moves, --yes answering
in advance, and without a tty and --yes it is an error.

Rerunning is always safe: a half whose work is done finds nothing
to do. A half that fails before its own push restores the repo it
touched via `jj op restore`.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
  -r, --revision <REV>
          The commit to publish, one: `@-` publishes the pair, any other a name
          alone [default: `@-`]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --bookmark <NAME>
          The remote's name for it: a bookmark on the line, moved there, one
          already at REV, or a new name, created there [default: the line's
          bookmark, or the one at REV]

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w|a`, its root or either
          repo, or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

  -y, --yes
          Pass the `--step` gates, and a forced push, without asking

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

I'd use the first: same title and body as reviewed, then the Land. Okay to run `vc-x1 commit -s b … --push`?
