content.content:
138	## Acquaint
139	
140	What a session does first, at its start and whenever the user says "acquaint" or "reacquaint",
141	in this order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#acquaint)):
142	
143	1. custom.md: when there is one, read it, and do what it asks for at acquaint
144	   ([custom.md](#custommd)).
145	2. Hooks: `bash agent-data/hooks.sh check`, and what it finds missing, different, or
146	   unregistered is reported for the user to install ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
147	3. Tools: `vc-x1 -V` and `vc-x1-dev -V`, both reported, and a dev build newer than the plain one
148	   is the user's to choose ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).
149	4. Repo check: look at each repo of the workspace for the four findings below, and report what is
150	   found before anything else. Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until
151	   the user says how to proceed.
152	   - Not up to date: a repo whose `main` is behind, ahead of, or diverged from its remote's, as
153	     the look reports it ([Sync](#sync)), run again with `--bookmark <bookmark>` when a cycle is
154	     in flight. A look that fails is reported as the check not made.
155	   - Uncommitted work: a work-repo `@` that is not empty, as `jj st` prints it. What the
156	     continuation notes account for, the notes themselves or a rung in flight they describe, is
157	     theirs to direct at step 5, and any other change is a finding. The agent-repo's `@` holds the
158	     session's own data and is never one.
159	   - Work off `main`: commits on a bookmark, a cycle's or any other, that do not descend from the
160	     remote's `main`. The user is told, and a rebase onto `main` is suggested.
161	   - Conflicts: a conflicted commit or working copy, as `jj st` and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'` show
162	     them. The acquaint stops there and the user is informed.
163	5. TODO.md: read the acquaint slice ([File
164	   reads](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)), the continuation notes first,
165	   each acted on, filed or kept, and the section reset ([Todo
166	   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
167	6. Report: say where things stand, the cycle in flight, its ladder in `zTOC.md`, or the top of `##
168	   Todo`, and wait.
169	
170	## Sync
171	
172	One command, `vc-x1 sync -s b`, brings both repos up to date, each `main` at the commit
173	its remote's `main` is at. It runs at the moments a cycle depends on `main`, and what it prints
174	is reported ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#sync)):
175	
176	- Acquaint looks: with `--dry-run`, which moves nothing, so each repo is reported as found.
177	- Opening syncs: as its first step, which is its rung's step 0, so the cycle's bookmark is
178	  created on an up-to-date `main`.
179	- Closing syncs: at its rung's step 0, so the record and version it carries are made from an
180	  up-to-date `main`. A rung between may sync at its step 0, the agent's or the user's call.
181	- Land syncs: as its first step, and a `main` the sync moved stops the Land.
182	
183	A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step until the user says how to proceed, as does
184	one at a rung's step 0 that moved a `main`, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask
185	for.
186	
187	## Cycle protocol
188	
189	How a [cycle](#terminology) runs ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-protocol)). Its record is
190	`TODO.md > ## In Progress` and nothing else ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)). The `.vc-config.md`
191	`[validate]` table defines the commands that validate the work-repo.
192	
193	### Cycles run on a bookmark
194	
195	A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, made first by `vc-x1 cycle --open` and named
196	by the cycle title's slug ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). `main`
197	advances only when the finished cycle lands on it, so development is never done on `main`, a
198	single-step cycle included. The agent-repo needs no bookmark. Commands in [Cycle
199	bookmarks](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), the long-lived case in [Long-lived
200	bookmarks][llb].
201	
202	### Cycle shape
203	
204	A cycle's shape is named at its closing, `--single-step` or `--multi-step`, and its branch's commit
205	count checks the name, so nothing is decided before the closing and nothing is guessed at it
206	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Every cycle has an opening and a closing, and the
207	shape says whether they are one commit.
208	
209	- Every cycle starts with `vc-x1 cycle --open`, which makes its bookmark on the work `@` and
210	  writes its record, a single-step cycle included. A cycle's first commit, by `cycle --commit`, is
211	  its opening, which the tool sees and no flag says.
212	- Single-step, no commit on the branch, the work in `@`: `cycle --close --single-step --body
213	  "..."` commits `@` as its one commit, under the bare cycle title, and it carries the opening's
214	  duties, the work, and the close-out's duties.
215	- Single-step, one commit, an opening committed first: `cycle --close --single-step` squashes the
216	  closing into it, `@` folded in, the title losing " opening" and gaining no " closing".
217	- Multi-step, a ladder: `cycle --close --multi-step` makes the closing commit, from the work `@` on
218	  the cycle's tip, over one commit or more, and is refused over none. Single-step is refused over
219	  two or more. `--trapezoid <target>` makes it the merge of the target and the tip, each revision
220	  listed, `cycle --close <REV,...>`, is another head joined, and `--land <target>` lands it in the
221	  same invocation.
222	- A ladder lands as a trapezoid, never squashed: every rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a
223	  squash discards all but one. Without `--trapezoid` the closing is linear, a plain commit on the
224	  ladder, which is the user's to ask for.
225	- The titles and bodies default. The opening's is the cycle title plus " opening" and `[opening]
226	  body`, a ladder's closing the title plus " closing" and `[closing] body`, and a single-step
227	  cycle's one commit gives its `--body`, since it holds the work. A work rung gives both.
228	- A dead end still closes and lands: a cycle abandoned after its opening keeps what is worth
229	  keeping, reverts the rest, and records what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it. Its
230	  closing is `cycle --close --multi-step --dead-end`, titled with the cycle title plus " dead-end
231	  closing".
232	
233	### Unplanned work
234	
235	Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
236	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):
237	
238	- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
239	- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.
240	
241	A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
242	first, as a jj commit with a local bookmark, never a patch file, so the inserted rung's commit
243	carries its own change alone, and they return once it is made.
244	
245	### Cycle-record
246	
247	A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
248	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).
249	
250	- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the rung subsections, the
251	  ladder over them being `zTOC.md`'s, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
252	  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
253	- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
254	  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
255	  the next opening.
256	  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
257	  - Its ladder, each rung with its marker, is `zTOC.md`'s, made by the tool from the rung headings
258	    under `#### Rungs` and rewritten into every cycle commit, each marker computed from the cycle's
259	    commits. It is kept by the closing so the landmark holds it and replaced by the next opening
260	    ([zTOC format](agent-data/notes.md#ztoc-format)).
261	  - Every commit of a cycle is a rung's: a commit whose title is no rung heading is refused, so an
262	    unplanned rung gets its heading before its commit.
263	  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
264	- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
265	  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
266	  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
267	- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
268	- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
269	  landmark.
270	- May be reworked while local: while a cycle's work commits are local and its agent `@` uncommitted,
271	  an earlier commit's record may be reworked. By default it is unnecessary, a later rung revising
272	  the record, and it is permitted when the error is significant, a word left to whoever is reading.
273	  A reworked commit's tree is validated again.
274	- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
275	  never left in the block.
276	- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.
277	
278	### Opening
279	
280	The cycle's first commit carries its plan: the record `cycle --open` scaffolds is deliberated and
281	laddered before it is committed, so the opening's review is of the plan, where a wrong direction
282	costs the least. The user is free to commit the setup first. A single-step cycle does all of it in
283	its one commit ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit
284	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):
285	
286	1. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), whatever the cycle's form.
287	2. Open: `vc-x1 cycle --open --title "<bare cycle title>"` makes the bookmark on the work `@`,
288	   kept local, first, so every edit of the cycle is on its branch. It then writes the record: what
289	   `## Closed` holds is deleted, the `## Todo` entry of that title is moved into the `## In
290	   Progress` scaffold ([The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block), the
291	   specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md)), and `zTOC.md`'s ladder is replaced
292	   with the opening and the closing.
293	3. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
294	   the rank it names.
295	4. Deliberate and plan: write the problem, the solution, the acceptance check, and the
296	   deliberation, and ladder the work rungs, each a `##### ` heading under `#### Rungs` with its
297	   intent. `vc-x1 cycle --ladder` makes the ladder from the headings. A small cycle's deliberation
298	   reads `_None._`, and the plan stays provisional, later rungs revising it.
299	5. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
300	   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), by the project's own tool, and the agent-files
301	   version with it when the cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
302	   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
303	
304	Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
305	bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).
306	
307	### The per-rung flow
308	
309	Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
310	immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)). `vc-x1 cycle
311	--status` says where the cycle stands and which rung is next:
312	
313	0. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), required at the opening and the closing, optional
314	   between, the agent's or the user's call.
315	1. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
316	   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), by the project's own tool, the agent-files
317	   version beside it in an `agent-files` proposal cycle. The version is the project's and `vc-x1`
318	   never writes it. With `[version]` in the config it refuses a commit that leaves the version
319	   unchanged, and `--same-version`, which commits anyway, is the user's to allow.
320	2. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
321	   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
322	3. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under `####
323	   Rungs`.
324	4. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
325	   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates. A failure is read and its cause
326	   named before validation runs again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported
327	   and given a Todo entry. A rung that changes the artifact then installs the working copy's dev
328	   build, `vc-x1 install --profile dev`, so the review runs the code under review, and again after
329	   each review fix ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). A rung has
330	   its own test and no more, the acceptance check being the closing's.
331	5. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message
332	   with no title or body. The review is of the working-copy diff ([jj
333	   basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)). Iterate over steps 2 through 5 until the user approves
334	   with "continue" or "go".
335	6. Describe: write the description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form),
336	   read from the file first with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md)
337	   ([Commit description](#commit-description)). A local description can still be changed before
338	   the Land, so it has no review of its own.
339	7. Commit: after approval, the work and agent repos are committed locally by `vc-x1 cycle --commit
340	   -s b --title "..." --body "..."`, a pair ([Committing vs pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)). The
341	   cycle's first commit is its opening and needs neither title nor body. The ladder is rewritten
342	   into the commit, the rung `(done)` and the next `(current)`, so no marker is typed or flipped.
343	   The closing is `vc-x1 cycle --close -s b` and its shape ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape),
344	   [Close-out](#close-out)). A rung that
345	   changes the artifact then installs its dev build again, so the next rung runs the committed
346	   code, not the working copy's ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).
347	
348	### Committing vs pushing
349	
350	A cycle's commits are made *by* `vc-x1 cycle`, a rung by `--commit` and the closing by `--close`,
351	never by `jj commit`, and published only by a push
352	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)).
353	
354	- `cycle --commit`, `--close`, and `--land` stay on this machine and need no approval. Each names
355	  its scope, `-s`, as every command that writes does: `b` the pair, `w` the work half, and `p` a
356	  plain repo.
357	- `--push` on any of them publishes, exactly like `vc-x1 push`, as does `squash-push`. With
358	  `--commit` or `--close` it is a draft push, of the cycle's bookmark, and with `--land` it is the
359	  publish, of the target.
360	- `vc-x1 squash` continues a rung, folding the working copy into it. `squash --title --body` is the
361	  sanctioned re-describe of `@-`. `vc-x1 commit` is the plain commit of a pair, for work outside a
362	  cycle, and `commit -r REV --title --body` describes a commit made by hand.
363	- A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders)
364	  intermediates, which collapse before the rung commits. What the commands do is in [vc-x1 commit
365	  and push][vpush].
366	
367	#### A cycle is local by default
368	
369	A cycle's commits stay on this machine until its Land, and the user decides when each side is
370	committed and when either is published, at any rung, every push still taking its own approval
371	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-cycle-is-local-by-default)).
372	
373	- The default: every commit is `vc-x1 cycle --commit -s b`, a pair, the agent commit holding the
374	  session to that moment, and the opening's bookmark created and not pushed.
375	- Any mix of work and agent commits is valid. `cycle --commit -s b` makes a 1:1 pair, `cycle
376	  --commit -s w` rungs then `commit -s a --covers <REVSET>` or the Land make N:1, and several agent
377	  commits naming one work commit make 1:M. The rule is the links: a work commit's `ochid:` names
378	  each agent change it pairs with, an agent commit's names each work commit it covers, each below
379	  an `orepo:`
380	  naming the other repo, and a squash folds into a commit an `ochid:` names, never that commit
381	  away, since jj keeps the change id of the commit squashed into ([Cross-repo
382	  linking](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
383	- A backup, a move between machines, or someone else to see the cycle publishes mid-cycle by a
384	  draft push, `push -s b`, and `-s w` rungs first get their agent commit, `commit -s a --covers
385	  <REVSET>`.
386	- The Land commits the agent `@` first, one `ochid:` per work commit it has not yet covered, none
387	  when every rung is a pair, an older work commit's `ocid:` and `pcid:` giving way to `orepo:`,
388	  trees unchanged.
389	
390	### Commit description
391	
392	The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
393	descriptions][cdd]).
394	The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), two plain paragraphs: no
395	version, file list, or deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).
396	
397	### Pushing
398	
399	Pushing is by `vc-x1 cycle --push -s b`, which publishes what the cycle's state calls for, a
400	draft's bookmark or a Land made here, by a stage's `--push`, or by `vc-x1 push`, and the Land's
401	bookmark moves are `cycle --land`'s and `delete-bookmark`'s.
402	
403	#### Before any push
404	
405	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))
406	
407	- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it. `vc-x1 push
408	  --yes` is for that approval alone, since an agent can type it as easily as anything else.
409	- A push that would be forced, a published commit rewritten, is asked about by `push` and
410	  `squash-push` and refused by `cycle` and `commit`, and the `--yes` flag answers, so the agent
411	  passes it only for a forced push the user approved.
412	- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
413	- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.
414	
415	#### At rest
416	
417	The contract that keeps the work-repo clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
418	item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest)):
419	
420	1. The agent publishes: a step that publishes is complete when its command is issued. The agent says
421	   what is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word
422	   "Published", and does nothing further until the user speaks.
423	2. Clean by squash-push: a Land is published by the agent only with the user's permission. A run of
424	   delegated cycles follows each `cycle --land --push` with the next cycle's opening, which carries
425	   the session's tail. A Land the agent made locally is published by the user after the session:
426	   `vc-x1 squash-push -s b` pushes the work target first, the shared repo and so the push likely to
427	   be refused, then folds the tail into the Land's agent commit and pushes it, so each `main` moves
428	   once, forward.
429	
430	"Clean" means the work `@` is empty, and once the user's squash-push has run the agent's `@` too.
431	Before it the agent's `@` is the session's data and no finding, as [Acquaint](#acquaint) says. A
432	late work-repo tweak after a push is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push ([vc-x1
433	commit and push][vpush]).
434	
435	### Close-out
436	
437	The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
438	does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):
439	
440	1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated, as the first thing in closing, and record
441	   pass or fail. A rung may run it and the closing record the result, since some checks run only
442	   mid-ladder. A failure is a finding, and why it failed is determined.
443	2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
444	   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A published rung
445	     title and the bookend pair keep their names, so a rename then reaches the block's text and the
446	     rungs not yet published only
447	   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
448	   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
449	   - complete the closing rung's subsection
450	   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
451	     belongs to
452	   - the block is moved whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
453	     `_No cycle currently in progress._`, and `zTOC.md`'s ladder is rewritten with every marker
454	     final, both by `vc-x1 cycle --close`.
455	3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
456	4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
457	   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
458	5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)): a ladder closes as a
459	   trapezoid, `cycle --close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid <target>`, the closing commit carrying
460	   the shape, so
461	   nothing is reshaped at Land.
462	6. Continuation notes: anything the next agent needs is written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation
463	   notes`, the first section, before the closing commit, which carries them, so the work-repo is
464	   clean from the Land on. A fact known only after the Land is not written: the note names what the
465	   next session checks, `main` at the closing, the bookmarks gone, the installed version's commit.
466	   The next acquaint reads it first, files or keeps each item, and resets the section ([Todo
467	   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
468	7. Test the closed cycle: the acceptance check again, as the last thing, on the closed tree. It is
469	   the first run on that tree when a merge brought the target's changes in, and otherwise a
470	   confirmation the user may skip. A fault found here stops the flow ([Stop and
471	   ask](#stop-and-ask)), and the way back is the user's choice: reopen the cycle, fix inside the
472	   closing, fix on top, or their own, the test itself being what may be wrong.
473	8. Land: on the user's go, the sequence in [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
474	   A Land is a fast-forward, and a target that moved is refused naming the ways on: a merge at the
475	   Land, `cycle --land <target> -s b --merge`, which the user asks for and which lands a tree no
476	   rung validated, the closing made again, or a rebase.
477	9. Restart: the user restarts the agent.
478	
479	### Local ladders
480	
481	A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
482	the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
483	`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),
484	[why](agent-data/rationale.md#local-ladders)).
485	
486	[cbt]: agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit
487	[cdd]: agent-data/prose.md#commit-titles-and-descriptions
488	[llb]: agent-data/jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged
489	[snn]: agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered
490	[vpush]: agent-data/jj.md#vc-x1-commit-and-push-what-they-do-and-do-not-do
491	
492	## Working practices

file.content:
## Acquaint

What a session does first, at its start and whenever the user says "acquaint" or "reacquaint",
in this order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#acquaint)):

1. custom.md: when there is one, read it, and do what it asks for at acquaint
   ([custom.md](#custommd)).
2. Hooks: `bash agent-data/hooks.sh check`, and what it finds missing, different, or
   unregistered is reported for the user to install ([Working practices](#working-practices)).
3. Tools: `vc-x1 -V` and `vc-x1-dev -V`, both reported, and a dev build newer than the plain one
   is the user's to choose ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).
4. Repo check: look at each repo of the workspace for the four findings below, and report what is
   found before anything else. Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until
   the user says how to proceed.
   - Not up to date: a repo whose `main` is behind, ahead of, or diverged from its remote's, as
     the look reports it ([Sync](#sync)), run again with `--bookmark <bookmark>` when a cycle is
     in flight. A look that fails is reported as the check not made.
   - Uncommitted work: a work-repo `@` that is not empty, as `jj st` prints it. What the
     continuation notes account for, the notes themselves or a rung in flight they describe, is
     theirs to direct at step 5, and any other change is a finding. The agent-repo's `@` holds the
     session's own data and is never one.
   - Work off `main`: commits on a bookmark, a cycle's or any other, that do not descend from the
     remote's `main`. The user is told, and a rebase onto `main` is suggested.
   - Conflicts: a conflicted commit or working copy, as `jj st` and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'` show
     them. The acquaint stops there and the user is informed.
5. TODO.md: read the acquaint slice ([File
   reads](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)), the continuation notes first,
   each acted on, filed or kept, and the section reset ([Todo
   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
6. Report: say where things stand, the cycle in flight, its ladder in `zTOC.md`, or the top of `##
   Todo`, and wait.

## Sync

One command, `vc-x1 sync -s b`, brings both repos up to date, each `main` at the commit
its remote's `main` is at. It runs at the moments a cycle depends on `main`, and what it prints
is reported ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#sync)):

- Acquaint looks: with `--dry-run`, which moves nothing, so each repo is reported as found.
- Opening syncs: as its first step, which is its rung's step 0, so the cycle's bookmark is
  created on an up-to-date `main`.
- Closing syncs: at its rung's step 0, so the record and version it carries are made from an
  up-to-date `main`. A rung between may sync at its step 0, the agent's or the user's call.
- Land syncs: as its first step, and a `main` the sync moved stops the Land.

A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step until the user says how to proceed, as does
one at a rung's step 0 that moved a `main`, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask
for.

## Cycle protocol

How a [cycle](#terminology) runs ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-protocol)). Its record is
`TODO.md > ## In Progress` and nothing else ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)). The `.vc-config.md`
`[validate]` table defines the commands that validate the work-repo.

### Cycles run on a bookmark

A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, made first by `vc-x1 cycle --open` and named
by the cycle title's slug ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). `main`
advances only when the finished cycle lands on it, so development is never done on `main`, a
single-step cycle included. The agent-repo needs no bookmark. Commands in [Cycle
bookmarks](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), the long-lived case in [Long-lived
bookmarks][llb].

### Cycle shape

A cycle's shape is named at its closing, `--single-step` or `--multi-step`, and its branch's commit
count checks the name, so nothing is decided before the closing and nothing is guessed at it
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Every cycle has an opening and a closing, and the
shape says whether they are one commit.

- Every cycle starts with `vc-x1 cycle --open`, which makes its bookmark on the work `@` and
  writes its record, a single-step cycle included. A cycle's first commit, by `cycle --commit`, is
  its opening, which the tool sees and no flag says.
- Single-step, no commit on the branch, the work in `@`: `cycle --close --single-step --body
  "..."` commits `@` as its one commit, under the bare cycle title, and it carries the opening's
  duties, the work, and the close-out's duties.
- Single-step, one commit, an opening committed first: `cycle --close --single-step` squashes the
  closing into it, `@` folded in, the title losing " opening" and gaining no " closing".
- Multi-step, a ladder: `cycle --close --multi-step` makes the closing commit, from the work `@` on
  the cycle's tip, over one commit or more, and is refused over none. Single-step is refused over
  two or more. `--trapezoid <target>` makes it the merge of the target and the tip, each revision
  listed, `cycle --close <REV,...>`, is another head joined, and `--land <target>` lands it in the
  same invocation.
- A ladder lands as a trapezoid, never squashed: every rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a
  squash discards all but one. Without `--trapezoid` the closing is linear, a plain commit on the
  ladder, which is the user's to ask for.
- The titles and bodies default. The opening's is the cycle title plus " opening" and `[opening]
  body`, a ladder's closing the title plus " closing" and `[closing] body`, and a single-step
  cycle's one commit gives its `--body`, since it holds the work. A work rung gives both.
- A dead end still closes and lands: a cycle abandoned after its opening keeps what is worth
  keeping, reverts the rest, and records what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it. Its
  closing is `cycle --close --multi-step --dead-end`, titled with the cycle title plus " dead-end
  closing".

### Unplanned work

Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):

- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.

A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
first, as a jj commit with a local bookmark, never a patch file, so the inserted rung's commit
carries its own change alone, and they return once it is made.

### Cycle-record

A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).

- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the rung subsections, the
  ladder over them being `zTOC.md`'s, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
  the next opening.
  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
  - Its ladder, each rung with its marker, is `zTOC.md`'s, made by the tool from the rung headings
    under `#### Rungs` and rewritten into every cycle commit, each marker computed from the cycle's
    commits. It is kept by the closing so the landmark holds it and replaced by the next opening
    ([zTOC format](agent-data/notes.md#ztoc-format)).
  - Every commit of a cycle is a rung's: a commit whose title is no rung heading is refused, so an
    unplanned rung gets its heading before its commit.
  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
  landmark.
- May be reworked while local: while a cycle's work commits are local and its agent `@` uncommitted,
  an earlier commit's record may be reworked. By default it is unnecessary, a later rung revising
  the record, and it is permitted when the error is significant, a word left to whoever is reading.
  A reworked commit's tree is validated again.
- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
  never left in the block.
- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.

### Opening

The cycle's first commit carries its plan: the record `cycle --open` scaffolds is deliberated and
laddered before it is committed, so the opening's review is of the plan, where a wrong direction
costs the least. The user is free to commit the setup first. A single-step cycle does all of it in
its one commit ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):

1. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), whatever the cycle's form.
2. Open: `vc-x1 cycle --open --title "<bare cycle title>"` makes the bookmark on the work `@`,
   kept local, first, so every edit of the cycle is on its branch. It then writes the record: what
   `## Closed` holds is deleted, the `## Todo` entry of that title is moved into the `## In
   Progress` scaffold ([The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block), the
   specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md)), and `zTOC.md`'s ladder is replaced
   with the opening and the closing.
3. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
   the rank it names.
4. Deliberate and plan: write the problem, the solution, the acceptance check, and the
   deliberation, and ladder the work rungs, each a `##### ` heading under `#### Rungs` with its
   intent. `vc-x1 cycle --ladder` makes the ladder from the headings. A small cycle's deliberation
   reads `_None._`, and the plan stays provisional, later rungs revising it.
5. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), by the project's own tool, and the agent-files
   version with it when the cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).

Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).

### The per-rung flow

Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)). `vc-x1 cycle
--status` says where the cycle stands and which rung is next:

0. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), required at the opening and the closing, optional
   between, the agent's or the user's call.
1. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), by the project's own tool, the agent-files
   version beside it in an `agent-files` proposal cycle. The version is the project's and `vc-x1`
   never writes it. With `[version]` in the config it refuses a commit that leaves the version
   unchanged, and `--same-version`, which commits anyway, is the user's to allow.
2. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
3. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under `####
   Rungs`.
4. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates. A failure is read and its cause
   named before validation runs again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported
   and given a Todo entry. A rung that changes the artifact then installs the working copy's dev
   build, `vc-x1 install --profile dev`, so the review runs the code under review, and again after
   each review fix ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). A rung has
   its own test and no more, the acceptance check being the closing's.
5. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message
   with no title or body. The review is of the working-copy diff ([jj
   basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)). Iterate over steps 2 through 5 until the user approves
   with "continue" or "go".
6. Describe: write the description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form),
   read from the file first with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md)
   ([Commit description](#commit-description)). A local description can still be changed before
   the Land, so it has no review of its own.
7. Commit: after approval, the work and agent repos are committed locally by `vc-x1 cycle --commit
   -s b --title "..." --body "..."`, a pair ([Committing vs pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)). The
   cycle's first commit is its opening and needs neither title nor body. The ladder is rewritten
   into the commit, the rung `(done)` and the next `(current)`, so no marker is typed or flipped.
   The closing is `vc-x1 cycle --close -s b` and its shape ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape),
   [Close-out](#close-out)). A rung that
   changes the artifact then installs its dev build again, so the next rung runs the committed
   code, not the working copy's ([Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)).

### Committing vs pushing

A cycle's commits are made *by* `vc-x1 cycle`, a rung by `--commit` and the closing by `--close`,
never by `jj commit`, and published only by a push
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)).

- `cycle --commit`, `--close`, and `--land` stay on this machine and need no approval. Each names
  its scope, `-s`, as every command that writes does: `b` the pair, `w` the work half, and `p` a
  plain repo.
- `--push` on any of them publishes, exactly like `vc-x1 push`, as does `squash-push`. With
  `--commit` or `--close` it is a draft push, of the cycle's bookmark, and with `--land` it is the
  publish, of the target.
- `vc-x1 squash` continues a rung, folding the working copy into it. `squash --title --body` is the
  sanctioned re-describe of `@-`. `vc-x1 commit` is the plain commit of a pair, for work outside a
  cycle, and `commit -r REV --title --body` describes a commit made by hand.
- A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders)
  intermediates, which collapse before the rung commits. What the commands do is in [vc-x1 commit
  and push][vpush].

#### A cycle is local by default

A cycle's commits stay on this machine until its Land, and the user decides when each side is
committed and when either is published, at any rung, every push still taking its own approval
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-cycle-is-local-by-default)).

- The default: every commit is `vc-x1 cycle --commit -s b`, a pair, the agent commit holding the
  session to that moment, and the opening's bookmark created and not pushed.
- Any mix of work and agent commits is valid. `cycle --commit -s b` makes a 1:1 pair, `cycle
  --commit -s w` rungs then `commit -s a --covers <REVSET>` or the Land make N:1, and several agent
  commits naming one work commit make 1:M. The rule is the links: a work commit's `ochid:` names
  each agent change it pairs with, an agent commit's names each work commit it covers, each below
  an `orepo:`
  naming the other repo, and a squash folds into a commit an `ochid:` names, never that commit
  away, since jj keeps the change id of the commit squashed into ([Cross-repo
  linking](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
- A backup, a move between machines, or someone else to see the cycle publishes mid-cycle by a
  draft push, `push -s b`, and `-s w` rungs first get their agent commit, `commit -s a --covers
  <REVSET>`.
- The Land commits the agent `@` first, one `ochid:` per work commit it has not yet covered, none
  when every rung is a pair, an older work commit's `ocid:` and `pcid:` giving way to `orepo:`,
  trees unchanged.

### Commit description

The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
descriptions][cdd]).
The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), two plain paragraphs: no
version, file list, or deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).

### Pushing

Pushing is by `vc-x1 cycle --push -s b`, which publishes what the cycle's state calls for, a
draft's bookmark or a Land made here, by a stage's `--push`, or by `vc-x1 push`, and the Land's
bookmark moves are `cycle --land`'s and `delete-bookmark`'s.

#### Before any push

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it. `vc-x1 push
  --yes` is for that approval alone, since an agent can type it as easily as anything else.
- A push that would be forced, a published commit rewritten, is asked about by `push` and
  `squash-push` and refused by `cycle` and `commit`, and the `--yes` flag answers, so the agent
  passes it only for a forced push the user approved.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.

#### At rest

The contract that keeps the work-repo clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest)):

1. The agent publishes: a step that publishes is complete when its command is issued. The agent says
   what is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word
   "Published", and does nothing further until the user speaks.
2. Clean by squash-push: a Land is published by the agent only with the user's permission. A run of
   delegated cycles follows each `cycle --land --push` with the next cycle's opening, which carries
   the session's tail. A Land the agent made locally is published by the user after the session:
   `vc-x1 squash-push -s b` pushes the work target first, the shared repo and so the push likely to
   be refused, then folds the tail into the Land's agent commit and pushes it, so each `main` moves
   once, forward.

"Clean" means the work `@` is empty, and once the user's squash-push has run the agent's `@` too.
Before it the agent's `@` is the session's data and no finding, as [Acquaint](#acquaint) says. A
late work-repo tweak after a push is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push ([vc-x1
commit and push][vpush]).

### Close-out

The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):

1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated, as the first thing in closing, and record
   pass or fail. A rung may run it and the closing record the result, since some checks run only
   mid-ladder. A failure is a finding, and why it failed is determined.
2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A published rung
     title and the bookend pair keep their names, so a rename then reaches the block's text and the
     rungs not yet published only
   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
   - complete the closing rung's subsection
   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
     belongs to
   - the block is moved whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
     `_No cycle currently in progress._`, and `zTOC.md`'s ladder is rewritten with every marker
     final, both by `vc-x1 cycle --close`.
3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)): a ladder closes as a
   trapezoid, `cycle --close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid <target>`, the closing commit carrying
   the shape, so
   nothing is reshaped at Land.
6. Continuation notes: anything the next agent needs is written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation
   notes`, the first section, before the closing commit, which carries them, so the work-repo is
   clean from the Land on. A fact known only after the Land is not written: the note names what the
   next session checks, `main` at the closing, the bookmarks gone, the installed version's commit.
   The next acquaint reads it first, files or keeps each item, and resets the section ([Todo
   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
7. Test the closed cycle: the acceptance check again, as the last thing, on the closed tree. It is
   the first run on that tree when a merge brought the target's changes in, and otherwise a
   confirmation the user may skip. A fault found here stops the flow ([Stop and
   ask](#stop-and-ask)), and the way back is the user's choice: reopen the cycle, fix inside the
   closing, fix on top, or their own, the test itself being what may be wrong.
8. Land: on the user's go, the sequence in [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
   A Land is a fast-forward, and a target that moved is refused naming the ways on: a merge at the
   Land, `cycle --land <target> -s b --merge`, which the user asks for and which lands a tree no
   rung validated, the closing made again, or a rebase.
9. Restart: the user restarts the agent.

### Local ladders

A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#local-ladders)).

content.content:
Manage tags

Usage: jj tag [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  delete   Delete existing tags [alias: d]
  list     List tags and their targets [alias: l]
  set      Create or update tags [alias: s]
  track    Start tracking given remote tags
  untrack  Stop tracking given remote tags

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global Options:
  -R, --repository <REPOSITORY>
          Path to repository to operate on
          
          By default, Jujutsu searches for the closest .jj/ directory in an ancestor of the current
          working directory.

      --ignore-working-copy
          Don't snapshot the working copy, and don't update it
          
          By default, Jujutsu snapshots the working copy at the beginning of every command. The
          working copy is also updated at the end of the command, if the command modified the
          working-copy commit (`@`). If you want to avoid snapshotting the working copy and instead
          see a possibly stale working-copy commit, you can use `--ignore-working-copy`. This may be
          useful e.g. in a command prompt, especially if you have another process that commits the
          working copy.
          
          Loading the repository at a specific operation with `--at-operation` implies
          `--ignore-working-copy`.

      --no-integrate-operation
          Run the command as usual but don't integrate any operations
          
          When this option is given, the operations will still be created as usual but they will not
          be integrated to the operation log. The working copy will also not be updated.
          
          The command will print the resulting operation ID. You can pass that to e.g. `jj --at-op`
          to inspect the resulting repo state, or you can pass it to `jj op restore` to restore the
          repo to that state. You can also pass the ID to `jj op integrate` to integrate the
          operation.
          
          Note that this does *not* prevent side effects outside the repo. For example, `jj git push
          --no-integrate-operation` will still perform the push.

      --ignore-immutable
          Allow rewriting immutable commits
          
          By default, Jujutsu prevents rewriting commits in the configured set of immutable commits.
          This option disables that check and lets you rewrite any commit but the root commit.
          
          This option only affects the check. It does not affect the `immutable_heads()` revset or
          the `immutable` template keyword.

      --at-operation <AT_OPERATION>
          Operation to load the repo at
          
          Operation to load the repo at. By default, Jujutsu loads the repo at the most recent
          operation, or at the merge of the divergent operations if any.
          
          You can use `--at-op=<operation ID>` to see what the repo looked like at an earlier
          operation. For example `jj --at-op=<operation ID> st` will show you what `jj st` would
          have shown you when the given operation had just finished. `--at-op=@` is pretty much the
          same as the default except that divergent operations will never be merged.
          
          Use `jj op log` to find the operation ID you want. Any unambiguous prefix of the operation
          ID is enough.
          
          When loading the repo at an earlier operation, the working copy will be ignored, as if
          `--ignore-working-copy` had been specified.
          
          It is possible to run mutating commands when loading the repo at an earlier operation.
          Doing that is equivalent to having run concurrent commands starting at the earlier
          operation. There's rarely a reason to do that, but it is possible.
          
          [alias: --at-op]

      --debug
          Enable debug logging

      --color <WHEN>
          When to colorize output
          
          [possible values: always, never, debug, auto]

      --quiet
          Silence non-primary command output
          
          For example, `jj file list` will still list files, but it won't tell you if the working
          copy was snapshotted or if descendants were rebased.
          
          Warnings and errors will still be printed.

      --no-pager
          Disable the pager

      --config <NAME=VALUE>
          Additional configuration options (can be repeated)
          
          The name should be specified as TOML dotted keys. The value should be specified as a TOML
          expression. If string value isn't enclosed by any TOML constructs (such as array
          notation), quotes can be omitted.

      --config-file <PATH>
          Additional configuration files (can be repeated)

The default can be configured via `revsets.git-push`. Use `--bookmark`/`--tag` to push specific
bookmarks or tags. Use `--all` to push all bookmarks and tags. Use `--change` to generate bookmark
names based on the change IDs of specific commits.

When pushing a bookmark or tag, the command pushes all commits in the range from the remote's
current position up to and including its target commit. Any descendant commits beyond the reference
are not pushed.

--

  -t, --tag <TAG>
          Push only this tag, or tags matching a pattern (can be repeated)
          
          If a tag isn't tracking anything yet, the remote tag will be tracked automatically.
          
          By default, the specified pattern matches tag names with glob syntax. You can also use
          other [string pattern syntax].

      --all
          Push all bookmarks and tags (including new ones)

          Push all tracked bookmarks and tags

          Push all deleted bookmarks and tags

  -r, --revision <REVSETS>

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='TODO.md'
s=open(p).read()
old_start=s.index("### chore: tag landed versions\n")
old_end=s.index("## Waiting")
block='''### chore: tag landed versions

#### Problem

zc-ring-x1 has no tags, so a dependent can pin it only by a path to a sibling checkout or by a raw
commit hash, neither saying which version it took. io-uring-x1 asks, on `m-12-0` in
`../vc-x1-messages`, for a tag per landed version, `v0.19.5` at `e705b50d` to start, the commit it
was built against, so it can write `tag = "v0.19.5"` in its git dependency.

#### Solution

Tag the two versions already landed, `v0.19.5` at `e705b50d` and `v0.19.6` at `4f8dc885`, and from
here on tag each Land's version on the commit `main` moves to, this cycle's `v0.19.7` the first.
The tags are made with `jj tag set` and published with `jj git push --tag` at the Land, beside
`main`, and a `custom.md` entry makes the tag a step of every Land. A reply on `m-12` names the
tags once they are published.

#### Acceptance check

`jj git push` has published the three tags, so `git ls-remote --tags origin` lists `v0.19.5` at
`e705b50d`, `v0.19.6` at `4f8dc885`, and `v0.19.7` at this cycle's landed commit, and a scratch
crate in `tmp/` depending on `zc-ring-x1 = { git = "https://github.com/winksaville/zc-ring-x1",
tag = "v0.19.5" }` passes `cargo check`.

#### Deliberation

- Single-step: the tree changes only by this record, the `custom.md` entry, and the version, and
  the tags are refs made at the Land, so one commit holds it all.
- Lightweight tags by jj, not annotated tags by git: jj 0.46 sets and pushes tags, `jj tag set`
  and `jj git push --tag`, so the jj-not-git rule holds, and jj makes lightweight tags only. A
  dependent's `tag =` resolves either kind, and the commit already carries the title and date.
- `v0.19.6` tagged too, though `m-12` names only `v0.19.5`: it is landed, its code the same as
  `v0.19.5`'s, and skipping it would leave a gap the moment the rule starts.
- No backfill before `v0.19.5`: no dependent asks for an older version, and the per-commit versions
  of earlier cycles would need each landmark found by hand.
- Tags published at the Land, not before: a cycle is local by default, and a tag on an unlanded
  commit names a version that may never land.
- The rule in `custom.md`: it is this project's because io-uring-x1 depends on it, and the set's
  Land has no tag step. We think a tag at every Land suits the family, which is an `agent-files`
  proposal and its own cycle, so it goes to `## Todo` rather than into `jj.md` here.
- The reply on `m-12` waits for the Land and for the messages clone's owner: `owner` shows a `take`
  by vc-x1 with no release after it, so writing the reply is the user's call when the time comes.
- `## Waiting` is `_None._`, nothing to promote.

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### chore: tag landed versions opening

The cycle's first commit, carrying its plan: the bookmark, the last cycle's record deleted, and the
Todo entry moved into this block.

##### chore: tag landed versions closing

Closing out the cycle.

'''
s=s[:old_start]+block+s[old_end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
sed -i '0,/^version = "0.19.6"/s//version = "0.19.7"/' Cargo.toml; grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml

content.content:
## Cycle bookmarks: create and land

The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).

**Create**, first at the cycle's opening: `vc-x1 cycle --open --title "<bare cycle title>"` makes
the bookmark on the work `@`, named by the title's slug (the anchor algorithm in [Markdown anchor
links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)), or `--bookmark <NAME>`, and kept local, then writes the
cycle's record. It refuses a name in use, locally or on `origin`, and a cycle already in progress,
`@` holding edits or not. The bookmark follows the change, so `vc-x1 cycle --commit` commits the
opening on it, and every later rung advances it and no other.

**Close**: `vc-x1 cycle --close -s b` with `--single-step` or `--multi-step`, from the work `@` on
the cycle's tip, makes the closing: a
ladder's closing commit, a merge of the target and the tip with `--trapezoid <target>`, or for a
single-step cycle the one commit, made from `@` or squashed into the opening, its `--body` given.
The target is read where it is now, so one that moved is joined. The record moves to `## Closed`
and the ladder is rewritten in the same commit.

**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Its `vc-x1
push` is the push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push), with the closing words
before it and silence after ([At rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest)):

1. Sync: `vc-x1 sync -s b`, and a `main` it moved stops the Land ([Sync](../AGENTS.md#sync)).
2. Integrate: `vc-x1 cycle --land <target> -s b`, local: it commits the agent `@` as the partner of
   the work commits that name it, none when every rung is a pair, fast-forwards the target, and
   deletes the cycle's local bookmark, every check made first. `--dry-run` says each step. The
   user may test here, before anything is published.
3. Publish: `vc-x1 push -s b --bookmark <target>`, the work repo first, the journal folded into the
   last agent commit while that is unpublished. `cycle --land <target> -s b --push` does steps 2 and
   3 as one, and `cycle --close --multi-step --land <target> -s b --push` the closing too.
   The agent publishes only with the user's permission, and otherwise the user does after the
   session, by `vc-x1 squash-push -s b` ([At rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest)).
4. Remote bookmark: `vc-x1 delete-bookmark -s w --bookmark <bookmark> --skip local`, when the topic
   was ever pushed.
5. Install: `vc-x1 build`, a `vc-x1 run -- -V` smoke check, and `vc-x1 install`, so the plain name
   is replaced only by what is on the target.

- `cycle --land` onto another cycle's bookmark, a stack of cycles landing together, is the command
  and not the sequence: nothing is installed, and the cycle is permanent only when the stack lands
  on its target.
- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.
- A Land fast-forwards by default, so what lands is the tree the closed cycle was tested as. A
  target that moved is refused naming the ways on: `--merge`, a merge at the Land, which the user
  asks for and which lands a tree no rung validated, the closing made again as a trapezoid, its
  merge joining the target where it is, or a rebase by `jj rebase`, every rung then validated again.

**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
- **A topic that was pushed is force-pushed**, under the same approval as any other push.

## Long-lived bookmarks: merge-only by default, deletable once merged
